notes: Curated currency for the authorities that carry the most corpus mass. Everything absent from this file resolves to 'unverified', which is a real answer and is labelled as one - it is not treated as 'in force'.

Matching is on the START of act_name or title, the same rule the repeal table uses. A circular that merely cites the Penal Code is not the Penal Code, and must not inherit its status in either direction.
Ranked by chunks in the corpus, counted from data/legal_kb/processed/chunks. That is corpus mass rather than observed retrieval frequency; no query log exists yet, and mass is the honest proxy.

'superseded' here means the instrument no longer governs new conduct. It does not mean the text is irrelevant: BNSS s.531 saves proceedings begun before 1 July 2024, so the repealed codes still govern conduct from before that date. The publication rules treat the two cases differently.

'saves_prior_conduct' marks an instrument whose repeal does not erase it: an offence committed before 1 July 2024 is still tried under the old codes, so they may still ground a published claim provided the repeal is stated. An instrument superseded without savings - a model manual replaced by a later edition - may not ground one at all, because there is no period it still governs.
